notes: An FM broadcast station carrying RDS, tuned to the station.
Not the house sample rate: 2.048 MS/s, because the multiplex runs to
57 kHz on a carrier that deviates 75 kHz and the discriminator wants
room for both.
This replaces a capture tuned to 89.6 while TSF sits at 89.5. That
offset was accidental, and it was quietly load-bearing: it exercised
the decoder's tolerance of a 100 kHz error with nothing written down
saying so, so a change that lost that tolerance would have failed here
for a reason nobody could name.
On-centre was measured rather than assumed to be better, because an FM
carrier at 0 Hz sits where the receiver's own DC spike is and that is a
real reason to tune off it. Two three-second captures of the same
station minutes apart: 89.5 read 19 groups agreeing, 89.6 read 18. No
penalty for being on the station.
Three seconds rather than two, and that is the part worth knowing. A
name is not one reading -- it is four two-character segments seen whole
twice and agreeing, since one pass through four segments can be four
segments of two different names. One second of this capture names
nothing. Two seconds names it, but a separate two-second recording made
minutes earlier did not: at two seconds it depends where the segment
cycle happens to fall. The old capture was on the lucky side of that
and check-pipelines has been passing on a coin flip. Three seconds is
margin rather than luck.
It decodes to programme identification 0x8343 and the programme service
name TSF. Three facts from three different places agree: the name, from
group 0A; the programme type, from block 2 of every group, which reads
'news' and TSF Radio Noticias is a news station; and the
identification's top nibble, 8, the country.
TSF is national and permanent, so this can always be recorded again.
